name: Wheal Fortune
summary: A tin and copper mine 3 km east of Redruth, flooded below 44 m.

performance.drainage: two horse whims (horse-driven winches) working rag-and-chain pumps, with horses in shifts day and night, lifting the water up to the adit
performance.inflow: about 140 liters a minute in summer, 230 to 270 in winter (Captain Tregonning's estimate)
performance.drainage_cost: about £12 a month in fodder and stable boys

flaws: The whims only just hold the water at 44 m; in a wet spell it rises
The richest tin and copper ore lies below about 48 m, under water
notes: The adit is a drainage tunnel at 22 m that drains by gravity to the valley, so pumps only need to lift the water up to it.
